item.title: Tehran strikes Iranian Kurdish base in Iraq with drones, report says
item.description:
Tehran strikes Iranian Kurdish base in Iraq with drones, report says

Iran's armed forces attacked bases belonging to an Iranian Kurdish opposition group in Iraq's Kurdistan region using drones, Mehr news agency reported.

"As part of a drone operation carried out by the Revolutionary Guards' ground forces, the headquarters of the terrorist and separatist group Komala, located in the Balisan region, was targeted last night," Mehr reported.

Earlier, Reuters reported that an explosive-laden drone attacked an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp northeast of Iraq's Erbil on Saturday night.

The semi-autonomous region hosts camps and bases belonging to several groups of Iranian Kurdish militants, which Iran has targeted repeatedly since the start of the Middle East war in February.

item.title: Morning update
item.description:
Morning update

Good morning, Middle East Eye readers,

If you are just joining us, here are the key developments from across the region and beyond:

* Israeli forces have sealed off all entrances to Hebron in the occupied West Bank and forcibly displaced around 2,200 Palestinians from their homes.

* US President Donald Trump has said Washington could strike Iran "as soon as tomorrow", or reach a “big, beautiful” agreement with Tehran.

* The Saudi-led coalition says it has intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile and two drones launched by the Houthis towards Riyadh.

* The Israeli army has said Palestinians with work permits will be barred from settlements in the occupied West Bank, except industrial zones and other approved areas, on Sunday and Monday.

* Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) spokesman Hossein Mohebbi has warned that the US-Israeli war against Iran could have consequences beyond the country’s borders, Press TV reported on Saturday.

* The Houthis have renewed their warning to airlines, airport staff and travellers against using Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport.

* Thousands gathered in Tel Aviv on Saturday for a large anti-government demonstration, three days ahead of a general election widely viewed as a referendum on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

* Russia’s embassy in Tehran has denied reports that its embassy staff and specialists working at the Bushehr nuclear power plant are preparing to leave Iran.

* An explosive-laden drone attacked an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp northeast of Iraq's Erbil on Saturday night, Reuters reported, citing security sources.

* Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has directed the judiciary to pursue compensation for "material and moral" damages caused by the US-Israeli war, state news agency IRNA reported.

* Iranian Speaker Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf will not attend the Brics parliamentary forum in New Delhi due to "certain unforeseen circumstances",  the Iranian embassy in India said on X.

item.title: Russia denies plans to evacuate staff working at Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant
item.description:
Russia denies plans to evacuate staff working at Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant

Russia’s embassy in Tehran has denied reports that Russian embassy staff and specialists working at the Bushehr nuclear power plant are preparing to leave Iran.

“Neither embassy staff nor Russian specialists at the Bushehr nuclear power plant have any plans to evacuate. Work continues as normal,” the embassy said in a statement, dismissing reports to the contrary as “FAKES”.

Bushehr, Iran’s only operating nuclear power plant, has come under repeated attack during the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran. Satellite imagery released in July showed damage inside the complex.

item.title: Rubio tells Cubans ‘now is the time’ to act to see political change
item.description:
US secretary of state makes comments after Trump tells US rally warships could intervene on return from Iran

Marco Rubio urged Cubans seeking political change in their country to act, saying “now is the time” moments after Donald Trump told a Friday rally for candidates in south Florida that US warships could intervene in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war.

The US secretary of state, in his social media post addressed “to those who seek to create positive change”, urged Cubans to capitalize on Trump’s plans. “The disappointment of failed promises, corruption, and the privileged lives of only a few; seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discrete [sic] partnership with the CIA,” Rubio said.
